report:
Email body and subject does not match

### Description

The header/subject of the email and the body reference two different monitors.
The body contains the correct reference.
![image](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/assets/9347753/17234ae3-b49e-4917-9ddc-bbf8872bcd91)
We only use email notifications, so I don't know if others might be experiencing the same issue.

### 👟 Reproduction steps

No idea, the only thing the monitors have in common is the notification.

### 👀 Expected behavior

The header/subject of the email should reference the correct monitor.

### 😓 Actual Behavior

The header/subject of the email references another monitor.

### 🐻 Uptime-Kuma Version

1.23.0

### 💻 Operating System and Arch

AMI2, Docker and Debian 11, Docker

### 🌐 Browser

Chrome 116.0.5845.188

evidence.quote: This was reported before and is likely because the Gmail client incorrectly groups emails with different subjects together.

confirmation.quote: Inspecting the original content of the email, ok, the subject is correct. ... I've changes the subjects to be "{{NAME}} is now {{STATUS}}!" and now it seams to work fine, so I guess because all the text was in brackets gmail thought it was related?

ambiguity: From the report alone this looks like D (subject template/notification code mixes up monitors, e.g. shared state between concurrent sends) or A (the mail client showing a different subject). Reporter explicitly says it is a single email with the wrong subject; the mail client is never named in the body.
decisive_code: server/notification-providers/smtp.js SMTP.send(): subject (msg or customSubject with {{NAME}} from monitorJSON) and body (msg + heartbeat time) are both built from the same msg/monitorJSON/heartbeatJSON arguments inside a single send() call and passed to one transporter.sendMail(); no shared/cached state, so the SMTP message cannot carry another monitor's name. The mismatch must come from the receiving client (Gmail conversation grouping).
notes: Closed by reporter, labeled cannot-reproduce; no code change. Later duplicate #6733 (title mentions GMail) got the same verdict from CommanderStorm.

reviews.decidable_why: Body shows a subject/body mismatch that reads like a templating bug; nothing in it points to Gmail threading.
smtp.js clearly builds the subject and body from the same monitor fields, so a code bug is unlikely. The Gmail threading explanation needs outside knowledge the body does not state.
